_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for operator commands in this flake.
One row here mints four things, so a command is declared once:
flake.nix         -> nix run .#<name>  (writeShellApplication, deps as runtimeInputs)
utils/<file>      -> the implementation, also runnable directly as ./utils/<file>
.nvim.lua / .exrc -> <leader>p<key>
utils/dev-help.sh -> the `hp` cheat-sheet, grouped and coloured
The groups and their order mirror the personal-servers flake, so moving
between the two projects does not mean relearning the menu. Groups that
have no counterpart there (storage, hardware, vm) come last.
Fields:
name     the nix run attribute and the binary name
file     the script under utils/ that implements it. SEVERAL ROWS MAY
SHARE ONE FILE: the script dispatches on the name it was
invoked as. dns-{status,off,on,test} are one script.
key      the <leader>p<key> suffix in Neovim; must be unique
group    which section of the cheat-sheet it appears under
order    position within that group
desc     one line, shown by nix run --help and the cheat-sheet
terse    short form for the narrow cheat-sheet column
deps     nixpkgs attribute names put on PATH for this command only
pythonDeps optional; nixpkgs python libraries built into an
interpreter for this command. `deps` cannot express these:
a library must be inside the interpreter to be importable.
A row using it must not also list python3.
prelude  optional; shared libraries under utils/lib/ inlined ahead of
the script (writeShellApplication wraps one file, so a
relative `source` cannot work)
sequence optional; the steps the command runs, printed as a banner
before it starts. Omit for read-only commands, which have no
workflow to announce and should not have their output
polluted.
usage    optional; the invocation including arguments, for the docs.
Omit when the command takes none.
excludeChecks optional; shellcheck codes tolerated for this script
Rows whose utils/<file> does not exist yet are skipped by the flake, so
this manifest describes the intended lifecycle while it is being built
out. `hp` marks those rows rather than hiding them.
`groups` fixes the order sections appear in. Without it the cheat-sheet
sorted them alphabetically — dns first, host fifth — which destroys the
lifecycle reading the grouping exists to give.

commands.name: create-host
commands.desc: Migrate a self-installed NixOS machine into this flake: read its hardware, write hosts/<name>/, register it and stage it
commands.terse: adopt this machine as a new host
sequence: refuse to run anywhere that is not the real machine
read hostId, disks, CPU/GPU and encryption off the running system
write hosts/<name>/, register it in fleet.nix and stage it for git

commands.name: update
commands.desc: Push this flake's configuration to one host, several, or all of them
commands.terse: rebuild a host (local, ssh or rsync)
sequence: resolve the targets and how each one deploys
build, and for remote hosts sign and copy the closure
activate, then offer to collect garbage (local only)

commands.name: update-all
commands.desc: Push this flake's configuration to every deployable host

commands.name: inventory
commands.desc: One line per host: role, owner, address, whether it answers, unit health

commands.name: preflight
commands.desc: Checks to run against a host before rebuilding it

commands.name: generate-hardware
commands.desc: Generate hardware.nix for a new host from the running machine
sequence: sudo nixos-generate-config --show-hardware-config
strip the parts this flake declares itself
write hosts/<hostname>/hardware.nix

commands.name: deploy
commands.desc: Create a Hetzner cloud server from hosts/<name>/server.nix and install onto it — the cloud path; gisnix install is the physical one
commands.terse: create a cloud server and install
sequence: check the host has hcloud parameters in server.nix
show the machine that would be created, and that it is billable
create it with hcloud, then install with nixos-anywhere

commands.name: check
commands.desc: One host in depth: reachability, boot phase, pool health, failed units

commands.name: install
commands.desc: Install a host onto a machine booted from a live ISO, over SSH, with nixos-anywhere and disko
sequence: check the host has a disko layout and that the target answers over SSH
name the machine, the address and the disk, and require the hostname typed back
partition and install with nixos-anywhere; --seed later clones the flake for its owner

commands.name: setup
commands.desc: Kartoza-branded setup wizard: partition a disk, create a host + user, and install (self-driven, for someone at the machine's own keyboard)
sequence: welcome, network check, new host or an existing host profile
hostname/locale/boot-theme, user account, storage (ZFS-encrypted by default)
confirm the default bundles, then confirm and install

commands.name: add-keyboard
commands.desc: Find a connected keyboard's device path and print a ready-to-paste kanata instance for it
commands.terse: wire up a new keyboard for kanata

commands.name: suspend
commands.desc: Suspend a host cleanly, leaving its pools in a resumable state

commands.name: wake
commands.desc: Wake a host over the network and wait for it to answer

commands.name: snapshot
commands.desc: Take an on-demand ZFS snapshot outside the sanoid schedule
sequence: list the datasets that would be snapshotted
confirm the label and the recursion
zfs snapshot, then report the new snapshots

commands.name: backup
commands.desc: Run the USB offload: send new snapshots to the backup pool
sequence: import the backup pool and check its health
send each dataset incrementally from its bookmark
update the bookmarks and export the pool

commands.name: reset
commands.desc: Destroy a host and reinstall it from scratch — guarded, irreversible
sequence: require the hostname typed back, and --i-mean-it
show exactly which pools and disks will be destroyed
destroy, then reinstall with deploy

commands.name: secrets
commands.desc: What secrets are declared, and which hosts and keys can decrypt them

commands.name: provision-secrets
commands.desc: Install the age identity on a host and rekey its secrets
sequence: confirm the target host and its age recipient
copy the identity to /root/.agenix/agenix.key
rekey the secrets that host is allowed to read

commands.name: unlock
commands.desc: Unlock an encrypted pool over initrd SSH so a host can finish booting

commands.name: add-site-deploy-key
commands.desc: Generate a deploy key and register it for a repository
commands.terse: mint and register a deploy key

commands.name: netbird-provision
commands.desc: Join a host to the company NetBird overlay, locally or remotely
commands.terse: enrol a host in the overlay
sequence: obtain a setup key for the company network
install and enable netbird on the target
verify the overlay address and its resolvers

commands.name: env
commands.desc: Show or switch this checkout between development and production mode

commands.name: dns-status
commands.desc: What is actually resolving: NetBird resolvers, blocky, upstream

commands.name: dns-off
commands.desc: Pause ad filtering for a while — it restores itself automatically
sequence: stop blocky
schedule a transient timer to start it again
report when filtering comes back

commands.name: dns-on
commands.desc: Restore ad filtering now, cancelling any pending auto-restore

commands.name: dns-test
commands.desc: Score how much advertising and tracking is being blocked

commands.name: test
commands.desc: Run the flake checks: host evaluation, shellcheck, per-host VM tests

commands.name: lint
commands.desc: Static analysis across the repo: nixfmt, shellcheck, statix, deadnix, reuse, gitleaks

commands.name: hooks
commands.desc: Install the pre-commit hooks into this working tree

commands.name: release
commands.desc: Cut a release: tag the deploy point and push it

commands.name: cleanup-orphans
commands.desc: Remove zfs-backup orphan snapshots from datasets outside the backup set
sequence: list datasets carrying zfs-backup snapshots
identify those outside the configured backup set
confirm, then destroy only the orphaned snapshots

commands.name: power
commands.desc: Profile this machine's heat and power draw and say what is costing it; also sets a temporary charge limit or low-power mode for travel

commands.name: keyboard-diagrams
commands.desc: Redraw the default kanata layout diagrams (base + navigation, one set per kanataLayout), then open the folder

commands.name: vm
commands.desc: Run any host's configuration in QEMU — quick boot by default, or --boot for the full UEFI/GRUB/Plymouth sequence
commands.terse: run a host in a VM

commands.name: create-win11-vm
commands.desc: Create a Windows 11 VM under libvirt with sensible defaults

commands.name: capture-boot
commands.desc: Capture a frame per second from a QEMU boot window, for boot-splash work

commands.name: configure
commands.desc: Turn a host's software bundles on and off, and edit what those bundles contain, from a menu built out of the bundle registry
sequence: read every bundle under software/, and what this host takes today
tick the bundles this machine should have; e edits what they contain
show the diff, write it if you agree, then evaluate and undo if broken

commands.name: bundles
commands.desc: What software bundles exist, what is in them, and what implies what
